declarations.name: request_mappings
declarations.label: Request Mappings
declarations.description: JSON array of mappings. Each entry is {"source_field", "target_field", "transform", "cast_to", "value"} where transform is one of direct, rename, type_cast, extract, constant and cast_to is one of string, integer, float, boolean. An empty array forwards request_data unchanged.

component.description:
What it does Sits between two components that do not agree on field names and translates one to the other. If the component upstream calls it customer_id and the one downstream expects id, this renames it in passing. No code, no redeploy.

How it works Reads the data travelling through it and applies a mapping table you supply. Each rule can copy or rename a field, change its type, pull a value out of a nested object, or inject a constant, and the result - exactly the fields the rules name, in order - replaces the data for the next component. With no table configured it forwards everything untouched, so it is safe to drop into a flow before you have configured it. A table that is not valid JSON, or a rule that is incomplete, fails the run with a message naming the rule; so does a value that cannot be cast, such as "abc" to integer. A source field that did not arrive is left out and logged.

Configure
- Request Mappings - the mapping table, written as JSON. Empty by default. Each entry has a target_field and a transform:
- direct or rename - copy source_field to target_field.
- type_cast - copy source_field, cast to cast_to: string, integer, float or boolean.
- extract - copy a nested value, with source_field a dotted path such as customer.address.city; null when the path is missing.
- constant - set target_field to value on every run.
Any entry may add cast_to.

In and out In: whatever the previous component sent. Out: the fields your mapping produces, or the same data when no mapping is configured. Any artifact is passed on untouched.

Use it when
- Two components you did not write need to talk to each other.
- Every request needs a constant injected, such as a tenant id or a model name.
- A downstream component needs a flat field that currently sits nested inside an object.
component.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: adapter
name: Data Adapter
description: >
  Reshapes request_data between two components that disagree on field names.
  A configured mapping table renames, casts, extracts nested values, or injects
  constants. With no table configured it forwards what it received unchanged.
  A malformed table, or a value that cannot be cast, raises and fails the run.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    # The artifact is forwarded straight into the Output constructor and is
    # never dereferenced, so it is welcome but never required -- optional(json)
    # is the only declaration that is true of this script.
    artifact_type_input: optional(json)
    artifact_type_output: optional(json)
    # Not `response_data_passthrough`: passthrough is true only while no
    # mapping table is configured, and becomes a false promise the moment one
    # is. The key set is configuration-determined in both branches.
    response_data_contract: dynamic
    response_data_contract_reason: >
      response_data keys are the `target_field` values of the mapping table
      configured in the `request_mappings` node parameter. When that parameter
      is empty the adapter forwards the inbound request_data key set unchanged.
      Either way the key set is fixed by node configuration, not by this script,
      so it cannot be enumerated statically.

input_parameters:
  - name: request_mappings
    type: text_long
    label: Request Mappings
    default: "[]"
    description: >
      JSON array of mappings. Each entry is
      {"source_field", "target_field", "transform", "cast_to", "value"} where
      transform is one of direct, rename, type_cast, extract, constant and
      cast_to is one of string, integer, float, boolean.
      An empty array forwards request_data unchanged.
component.name: DATA ADAPTER (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)

ports.label: Input
ports.response_data_contract_reason: response_data keys are the `target_field` values of the mapping table configured in the `request_mappings` node parameter. When that parameter is empty the adapter forwards the inbound request_data key set unchanged. Either way the key set is fixed by node configuration, not by this script, so it cannot be enumerated statically.

component.short_description: Translates field names and types between two components that disagree, with a mapping table and no code.
